questions.q: Do you play any video games?
questions.answer: Occasionally, mostly simple ones on my phone to pass the time. I'm not a serious gamer by any means. For me it's more of a light [[distraction]] during a break than a proper hobby.

questions.q: What games did you play when you were a child?
questions.answer: Mostly outdoor games with the neighbourhood kids, like hide and seek, kabaddi and, of course, cricket. We spent long, [[carefree]] afternoons outside, and nobody needed a screen to have a good time.

questions.q: Do you enjoy playing board games?
questions.answer: I do, especially carrom, which is hugely popular in Bangladesh. My family sometimes plays after dinner, and it gets surprisingly [[cut-throat]], particularly between me and my younger sister, who absolutely hates losing.

questions.q: Do adults in your country play games?
questions.answer: Quite a lot, actually. Older men often gather at tea stalls to play cards or chess in the evenings, and ludo on mobile phones has become a national [[pastime]] for people of all ages.

questions.q: Do you think video games are good for children?
questions.answer: In moderation, they can be. Some games genuinely improve problem-solving and reaction speed. The real issue is when children play for hours on end, because it can become quite [[addictive]] and take time away from studying and being outdoors.
